PRENATAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Prenatal screening for common trisomies
Gestational Age at Sampling: 17 weeks
Procedure: Amniocentesis

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Methodology: Multiplex QF-PCR analysis of uncultured amniotic fluid cells using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: NORMAL
D13S631: 1.0:1.1
D13S258: 1.0:1.0
D13S742: 1.1:1.0

Chromosome 18: NORMAL
D18S391: 1.0:1.1
D18S390: 1.0:1.0
D18S535: 1.1:1.0

Chromosome 21: NORMAL
D21S1435: 1.0:1.0
D21S1411: 1.0:1.1
D21S1446: 1.1:1.0

CONCLUSION
PCR analysis consistent with normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18 and 21. No abnormality detected.

INTERPRETATION
The QF-PCR results indicate a normal chromosomal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 in this fetal sample. The peak area ratios for all informative markers fall within the normal diallelic range (0.8-1.4), excluding trisomy for the tested chromosomes.

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect complete trisomies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. It will not detect:
- Chromosomal mosaicism below 20%
- Structural chromosomal abnormalities
- Segmental imbalances
- Abnormalities of other chromosomes
- Single gene disorders

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis required on this sample based on these results.

Authorized by: [redacted name], PhD
Consultant Clinical Scientist
[redacted date]
